ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is quadrilateral WXYZ, with W at the top, X on the right, Y at the bottom, and Z on the left; diagonal ZX passes horizontally through the interior, diagonal WY passes vertically through the interior, and the two lines intersect at U. The figure is symmetric about the horizontal diagonal ZX, so W and Y are a pair of symmetric non-axis vertices. Reasoning: Given m∠WXY = 120, m∠WZY = 4x, and m∠ZWX = 10x. By the symmetry of the kite shape, angle W and angle Y are equal, so m∠ZYX = m∠ZWX = 10x. The sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°, so 120 + 4x + 10x + 10x = 360. Combining gives 120 + 24x = 360, 24x = 240, x = 10. Therefore m∠ZYX = 10x = 100.

method.method_draft: Decompose the kite into two isosceles triangles sharing diagonal WY. From the diagram, read the side-pair structure of the kite as ZW = ZY and XW = XY, with diagonal WY splitting the figure into triangles WXY and WZY. From the text, ∠WXY = 120, ∠WZY = 4x, and the whole top angle ∠ZWX = 10x. In triangle WXY, since XW = XY, it is isosceles with vertex angle 120 at X, so the base angles at W and Y are each (180 - 120)/2 = 30. In triangle WZY, since ZW = ZY, it is isosceles with vertex angle 4x at Z, so the base angles at W and Y are each (180 - 4x)/2 = 90 - 2x. The whole angle at W is ∠ZWX = ∠ZWY + ∠YWX = (90 - 2x) + 30 = 10x. Solve x = 10. Then the desired angle at Y is ∠ZYX = ∠ZYW + ∠WYX = (90 - 2x) + 30 = 100.
